done_when: forge upgrade treats an earlier upgrade fix whose pull request has merged as finished: it removes that fix's leftover worktree and local branch (only when they hold nothing unpushed) and carries on; an earlier upgrade fix that is still open, or has unpushed work, still refuses as today; a command test covers a repo adopted on an earlier release upgrading twice with the first fix's worktree left behind, plus the unpushed-work refusal

findings.body: The cleanliness check omits ignored files. If a merged upgrade checkout contains an ignored `.env` or `data/rows.csv`, it passes this guard and is deleted, losing local data that was never pushed. Omitting `--force` does not protect it: [Git's implementation](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.48.0/builtin/worktree.c#L1182-L1281) checks ordinary status and then recursively deletes the directory. This violates “data is protected against loss.” Existing cleanup in `src/forge/doctor.py:74–77` includes ignored files and permits only recognised caches. Apply equivalent protection here and extend the command refusal test to preserve ignored configuration and data files; the current untracked-file case cannot detect this loss.
findings.title: Standard: data is protected against loss

why: forge upgrade refuses with 'The upgrade to vX is still open in fix upgrade-forge-to-vX' when that earlier upgrade fix's pull request has merged and only its worktree was left behind (reported by a client session upgrading to v1.2.8)
